memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: Both frames ground compensation in total burden, actual time, and modality-neutral treatment, while covering incomplete and repeated studies and recognizing omitted out-of-session work. They differ on whether proposal-stage payment flexibility requires an equity explanation, and each adds distinct payment or cost-classification provisions.

relations.reason: Both state the same budgeting rule; the compared frame merely specifies technical and travel preparation within the broader preparation burden.
relations.summary: Compensation budgets should reflect estimated participation burden, including session time and required preparation.

relations.reason: The claims jointly make burden, rather than study modality itself, the basis for equal base rates and justified compensation differences.
relations.summary: Compensation should remain modality-neutral at equal burden while accounting for extra travel or technical burden when present.

relations.reason: The operational rule and scope are the same in both frames.
relations.summary: Actual time spent in sessions should be compensated regardless of research modality.

relations.reason: This independently useful payment-method option appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Cash should remain an available payment method for face-to-face studies.

relations.reason: The shared proposal-stage flexibility is preserved, while the reference claim states a condition absent from the compared claim.
relations.summary: An unresolved payment method need not be treated as a proposal-stage deficiency, with the reference frame explicitly requiring an equity explanation.

relations.reason: Both express the same fairness principle; technical preparation is a specific form of the preparation burden named in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Participants assess compensation fairness from combined session, travel, and preparation burdens.

relations.reason: Rescheduling and return visits on one side and diary or reporting work on the other are complementary applications of the same repeated-study compensation policy.
relations.summary: Compensation for repeated or longitudinal studies should include consequential burdens beyond individual session attendance.

relations.reason: Prototype-caused termination and participant withdrawal are compatible termination circumstances governed by the same actual-time principle.
relations.summary: Participants should be paid for time already invested when participation ends before study completion.

relations.reason: Between-session preparation, advance setup, and follow-up reporting are complementary manifestations of the same omission tendency.
relations.summary: The described compensation practice tends to count session time while omitting participant work performed outside sessions.

relations.reason: This independently useful remote payment alternative appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Equivalent-value gift cards may be issued to remote participants unable to use electronic transfers.

relations.reason: This cost-classification rule appears only in the compared frame and is independent of its participant payment-method provision.
relations.summary: Participant research compensation should be distinguished from labor costs for field staff performing assigned support duties.

reports.both: Both use total burden and actual participation time to guide compensation, adjust for modality-related burdens, cover incomplete and repeated participation, and flag omitted out-of-session effort.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame permits equivalent gift cards for some remote participants and separates participant compensation from field-staff labor costs.
reports.differences: Proposal-stage payment-method flexibility is explicitly conditional on explaining equity in the reference frame but unconditional in the compared frame.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame preserves cash as an option for face-to-face studies.
